prompt: A European e-bike maker is deciding whether to enter the US market. The candidate's framework: (1) US demand for e-bikes; (2) Competitors and their market shares; (3) Costs of distribution, marketing and import duties. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: competitors' shares are part of US demand
options.feedback: Demand is how much US buyers want e-bikes; competitors' shares are how that demand is split. They are separate questions.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: costing comes after the decision to enter
options.feedback: Distribution, marketing and duties decide whether entry would pay, so they are part of the decision.

options.text: Missing: whether this client can beat US competitors
options.feedback: Right. The framework sizes the market, the rivals and the costs, but never asks whether this client can compete in the US: brand, channels and product fit.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: it only covers revenue and costs
options.feedback: It isn't a profit tree. Demand and competitors are market-entry buckets. What's missing is the client's ability to win.

explanation: Entry needs market attractiveness, competition, economics and the client's ability to win. Here the last one is missing.

extras.corrected_framework: US demand; competition; economics of entry; the client's ability to win (brand, channels, product fit)
